figures.finding: Vietnam's Law on Cinematography (2022) provides a Cinematographic Development Support Fund, an off-budget state fund, to support experimental films, debut films and young authors' films and films at festivals abroad; as of June 2026 the fund had yet to be implemented, so no share, cap or selection rate exists.

value.name: Cinematographic Development Support Fund (Quỹ hỗ trợ phát triển điện ảnh)

sources.said: The Cinematographic Development Support Fund is an off-budget state financial fund supported by the State with charter capital … Section 43. The Cinematographic Development Support Fund aims to: 1. Provide support for projects on experimental films, debut films, and films of young authors. 2. Provide support for authors, film production projects, and outstanding Vietnamese films that participate in film festivals, film awards, film competitions, film fairs, film programs, and film weeks abroad.
Although the Vietnam Film Fund was included in the 2006 Cinema Law and further expanded in the revised Cinema Law in 2022, it has yet to be implemented.

figures.finding: Vietnam has no production rebate: the Law on Cinematography says only that foreign organisations filming in Vietnam or using Vietnamese production services 'may receive tax incentives according to laws on tax'; a VAT refund for foreign film crews was proposed in a draft Law on Cultural Industry Development, due before the National Assembly in October 2026 (not confirmed passed).

proposed.measure: VAT refund for foreign film crews
proposed.instrument: draft Law on Cultural Industry Development
proposed.status: draft, scheduled for the October 2026 sitting

figures.applies: Vietnam, foreign productions; as of September 2026.

sources.said: Article 41. Incentive regulations for foreign organizations using film production services in Vietnam Foreign organizations producing films with the use of backgrounds in Vietnam or film production services provided by Vietnamese organizations may receive tax incentives according to laws on tax.

Vietnam is considering a package of new incentives for the cultural industries, including VAT refunds for foreign film crews shooting in the country, as lawmakers review a draft Law on Cultural Industry Development ahead of its expected passage in October.
